courseTitle: How IT Teams Work: Agile, Waterfall, Scrum, Kanban & Software Releases

slots.practicalActivity: Pick a real feature you'd want built for a Databricks/Lakehouse team (e.g. 'a daily job that loads yesterday's sales CSVs into a Bronze Delta table') and decide whether a Waterfall or Agile approach fits it better, writing 2-3 sentences justifying the choice; then write 3 user stories for that same feature in the 'As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]' shape, each with at least one concrete acceptance criterion.
slots.deliverable: A short written Agile-vs-Waterfall justification for one real data-pipeline feature, plus 3 user stories with acceptance criteria for that feature.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a real Kanban board (a free Trello board or GitHub Projects board is fine) with Backlog, To Do, In Progress, Review, and Done columns, and place the 3 user stories from the previous slot onto it, moving one into To Do; then write a short note mapping each of those stories to what would happen to it in Dev, QA, UAT, and Production specifically for a data-pipeline change (e.g. what 'QA' means for a notebook that loads a Delta table versus a UI feature).
slots.deliverable: A real, screenshot-able Kanban board holding the 3 stories, plus a written Dev/QA/UAT/Prod walkthrough for one of those stories applied to a data-pipeline change.

slots.practicalActivity: Create a free GitHub repository, clone it locally, create a branch named after one of your user stories, add a text file describing the change, commit it with a real descriptive message (not 'fixed stuff'), push the branch, and open a pull request against main; then write a short release checklist (approval, monitoring, rollback plan, release notes) for what merging that PR into a production notebook pipeline would actually require.
slots.deliverable: A real GitHub repo with a branch, a commit, a pushed branch, and an open pull request, plus a written release checklist for deploying that change to a production pipeline.

slots.practicalActivity: Start the Castlebridge Retail capstone: break the sales director's one-paragraph request into at least 3 user stories (revenue-by-region, revenue-by-category, automatic refresh) with concrete acceptance criteria, build a Kanban board with Backlog through Done columns and place the stories on it, and write a short QA test plan for one story that includes at least one edge case (e.g. a region with zero sales for the month).
slots.deliverable: 3+ capstone user stories with acceptance criteria, a populated Kanban board, and a written QA test plan covering at least one edge case.

slots.practicalActivity: Finish the Castlebridge Retail capstone: write a one-paragraph UAT sign-off in the sales director's voice (approving the work or sending back specific feedback against the acceptance criteria from the previous slot), write a short, specific release note (what shipped, why, and any known limitation), and write up how you'd investigate and what you'd communicate to the regional manager for a simulated production incident where last month's numbers show as zero for one region.
slots.deliverable: A written UAT sign-off, a specific release note, and a documented incident-response writeup (investigation steps plus stakeholder communication) closing out the capstone.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can speak and work the way a real IT team does -- writing user stories with acceptance criteria, tracking work on a Kanban board, using Git for version control, and understanding the Dev/QA/UAT/Production chain and CI/CD release process every later course's hands-on pipeline and notebook work will move through.
